what: 7. Reconstruction QC: does the autoencoder generalize to real data?
title: Getting started with classydms
text: critical check classification: feed real samples full autoencoder (encoder + decoder) visually compare reconstructions originals. reconstructions look similar originals, encoder learned features transfer synthetic real. reconstructions blank smeared, synthetic distribution didn’t match real closely enough pretraining. healthy reconstructions look like: Peak locations reconstruction match peak locations original. Bright spots appear right (RT, CV) coordinates, even intensities dampened. overall layout — signal concentrated vs. ’s sparse — preserved. Mean MSE across samples low (typically < 0.05 normalized data). Warning signs: Reconstructions uniformly blank near-zero everywhere → encoder collapsed outputting average image Reconstructions peaks completely wrong locations → encoder didn’t learn spatial structure specific samples much higher MSE rest → samples morphological outliers (often worth flagging QC) reconstructions look poor, proceed classification — encoder features won’t meaningful. Common causes fixes: Synthetic-real distribution gap: re-check synthetic_quality_check() (see vignette("pretraining")), adjust dust_threshold size_jitter Insufficient training: increase steps_per_epoch * epochs retrain Encoder mode collapse: check encoder feature variance meaningful (channels vary across samples)
code: # Reconstruct a handful of real samples through the trained autoencoder recon <- reconstruct_real_samples(   autoencoder    = pretrain_result$autoencoder,   Z_list         = Z_padded,   sample_indices = 1:6 )  # Side-by-side heatmaps: row 1 = real, row 2 = reconstruction par(mfrow = c(2, 6), mar = c(1, 1, 2, 1)) for (r in recon) {   image(t(r$original)[, nrow(r$original):1],         col = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),         axes = FALSE,         main = paste0("real #", r$index)) } for (r in recon) {   image(t(r$reconstructed)[, nrow(r$reconstructed):1],         col = hcl.colors(100, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE),         axes = FALSE,         main = sprintf("recon (MSE=%.3f)", r$mse)) } par(mfrow = c(1, 1))  # Aggregate MSE across all samples all_recon <- reconstruct_real_samples(pretrain_result$autoencoder,                                        Z_padded,                                        sample_indices = seq_along(Z_padded)) mse_per_sample <- sapply(all_recon, function(r) r$mse) summary(mse_per_sample)

code: library(classydms)  # 1. Load raw data (samples_keep, y_keep) using your project-specific loader # 2. Preprocess samples_proc <- lapply(samples_keep, process_one_sample) b_list <- lapply(samples_proc, function(s) trim_bounds_from_occupancy(s$Z)) R0 <- max(sapply(samples_proc, function(s) nrow(s$Z))) C0 <- max(sapply(samples_proc, function(s) ncol(s$Z))) global_b <- pooled_trim_bounds(b_list, R = R0, C = C0) samples_trimmed <- lapply(samples_proc, trim_sample, bounds = global_b)  Z_norm   <- purrr::map(samples_trimmed, ~normalize_sample(.x$Z)) pad_dims <- compute_pad_targets(Z_norm) Z_padded <- purrr::map(Z_norm, ~pad_to_target(.x, pad_dims$H, pad_dims$W))  # 3. Estimate peak parameters from real data (label-agnostic) Z_raw     <- purrr::map(samples_trimmed, ~.x$Z) Z_pretrim <- purrr::map(samples_trimmed,                           ~if (!is.null(.x$Z_pretrim)) .x$Z_pretrim else .x$Z) peak_params <- estimate_peak_params(Z_raw, Z_pretrim_list = Z_pretrim,                                      top_k = 150, frac_height = 0.5)  # 4. Self-supervised pretraining (recommended: online, for memory efficiency) pretrain_result <- pretrain_denoising_online(   peak_params,   H = pad_dims$H, W = pad_dims$W,   steps_per_epoch = 1000L, epochs = 50L, batch_size = 32L,   save_path = "encoder.pt" )  # 5. Classify with elastic net on encoder features elnet <- cv_encoder_elastic_net(pretrain_result$encoder,                                  Z_list = Z_padded, y = y_keep,                                  k = 5, alpha = 0.5) elnet$auc elnet$coefs    # which of the 64 channels matter  # 6. Spatial saliency map for biomarker localization disease_idx <- which(y_keep == 2) orig_dims <- lapply(samples_trimmed, function(s) c(H = nrow(s$Z), W = ncol(s$Z))) sal <- aggregate_saliency_masked(pretrain_result$encoder, Z_padded,                                    coefs = elnet$coefs,                                    sample_indices = disease_idx,                                    orig_dims = orig_dims) # sal is a 2-D matrix in padded image coordinates; map back to RT/CV using # samples_trimmed[[1]]$time and samples_trimmed[[1]]$cv

H, W Output image dimensions. add_noise TRUE, add spatially-varying background noise. size_jitter Per-peak random log-normal scale factor SD size diversity. Default 0.15 (multiplicative variation roughly x1.16 / :1.16), matches typical GC-DMS peak-size variability value used getting-started vignette. Larger values regularize produce peaks noticeably larger smaller observed peak, biologically plausible; use pretraining stability requires . location_mode sample peak (RT, CV) locations.
